from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), Flash(warden_choice))

        self.place_at_grid(bender, 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), FadeIn(prisoner), FadeIn(bender))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "64 squares are represented by 6 binary bits.",
            "Bit positions 0 through 63 define every square.",
            "XOR parity acts as our digital checksum."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Binary Encoding", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load asset
        chessboard = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/chessboard.svg")
        self.place_in_area(chessboard, "A2", "C5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(chessboard)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display binary numbers 0 and 1. Color: #00FFFF (0), #FF00FF (1).
        bit0 = Text("0", font_size=40, color="#00FFFF")
        bit1 = Text("1", font_size=40, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(bit0, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(bit1, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(bit0), Write(bit1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00") 
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize bit sequence construction.
        sequence = VGroup(*[Text(str(x), color="#FFFFFF") for x in [1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1]]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(sequence, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(sequence))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00") 
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the parity bit concept.
        parity_bit = Text("1", color="#FF5733")
        parity_label = Text("Parity", font_size=18, color="#FF5733")
        parity_group = VGroup(parity_bit, parity_label).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_at_grid(parity_group, "D4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(parity_group), sequence.animate.set_color("#FF5733"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Target square index is encoded into board parity.",
            "Calculate XOR sum of all Heads positions.",
            "Flip the one coin to match target index.",
            "This ensures board parity equals target square.",
            "Information is hidden within coin state distribution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Information Strategy", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        coin_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg")
        board_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/board.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(board_icon, "B4", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(board_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        xor_sum = Text("101010", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(xor_sum, "A3")
        self.play(Write(xor_sum))
        self.place_at_grid(coin_icon, "A5", scale_factor=0.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(coin_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Flip coin
        self.play(coin_icon.animate.rotate(PI))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        new_xor = Text("000001", font_size=24, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(new_xor, "A3")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(xor_sum, new_xor))
        
        checkmark = Tex(r"$\checkmark$", color="#00FF00", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(checkmark, "D5", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(checkmark))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Flipping one coin changes exactly one parity bit.",

            "Proof confirmed: always identify the secret square."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Mathematical Proof via Parity", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup visuals: Input bits (4x4 example)
        bits = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=WHITE).add(Text(str(i % 2), font_size=20)) for i in range(16)])
        bits.arrange_in_grid(4, 4, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(bits, 'A2', 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(bits))
        
        # Asset: coin.svg
        coin = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coin.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(coin, 'B2', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Flash(coin, color="#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        xor_rect = Rectangle(width=2.2, height=2.2, color="#FFFF00").move_to(bits.get_center())
        self.play(Create(xor_rect))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Information Theory Significance", [
            "Strategy applies Error Correction Code principles.",
            "Information theory minimizes uncertainty via parity.",
            "Technology uses this to fix data corruption."
        ])
        
        phone_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Strategy applies Error Correction Code principles.
        # Display a QR code (simulated) next to a phone icon.
        qr_code = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE).set_fill(WHITE, opacity=0.3)
        phone = SVGMobject(phone_path).scale(0.5)
        qr_group = VGroup(qr_code, phone).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(qr_group, 'A3', 'B5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(qr_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Information theory minimizes uncertainty via parity.
        # Formula for uncertainty/parity bit
        formula = MathTex(r"H = -\\sum p_i \\log p_i", color=TEAL)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B3', 'C5', scale_factor=0.9)
        parity_bit = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#00FFFF").set_fill("#00FFFF", opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(parity_bit, 'A4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(formula), FadeIn(parity_bit))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Technology uses this to fix data corruption.
        # Final summary text fading in with a bright white background glow, appearing alongside phone.
        data_block = Rectangle(height=1.0, width=1.5, color=GREEN)
        label = Text("Error-Corrected Data", font_size=16)
        data_group = VGroup(data_block, label).arrange(DOWN)
        phone_2 = SVGMobject(phone_path).scale(0.4)
        final_group = VGroup(data_group, phone_2).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_in_area(final_group, 'D3', 'E5', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        glow = BackgroundRectangle(final_group, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(glow), FadeIn(final_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Impossible Chessboard: Decoding Information Theory

sections.title: The Hook: The Warden's Challenge
sections.content: Introduce the puzzle: A warden places 64 coins (Heads/Tails) on a chessboard. A prisoner must identify one specific square chosen by the warden after flipping exactly one coin. We establish the goal: How can the prisoner guarantee a win?
sections.example: A prisoner and a robot accomplice (Bender) are faced with a 8x8 grid of coins.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Binary Encoding
sections.content: Introduce the concept of bit-strings. Explain that a square's position (0-63) can be represented by 6 bits (2^6 = 64). Explain the XOR (parity) operation as a 'digital checksum'.
sections.example: Visualizing 64 squares as indices 000000 to 111111; demonstrating XOR on binary digits.

sections.title: The Information Strategy
sections.content: Explain that the prisoner needs to encode the target position into the parity of the board. The strategy: The XOR sum of all 'Heads' positions must match the target square's index.
sections.example: If the current XOR sum is 101010 and the target is 000001, we flip the coin that changes the sum to 000001.

sections.title: Mathematical Proof via Parity
sections.content: Demonstrate why flipping one coin changes exactly one bit in the parity sum, allowing the prisoner to correct the board state to perfectly match the target index.
sections.example: A Venn diagram animation showing how flipping a coin at position 'i' alters the global parity checksum.

sections.title: Conclusion: Information Theory Significance
sections.content: Summarize that this is an application of Error Correction Codes (ECC). Information isn't just about data; it's about minimizing uncertainty through parity bits.
sections.example: Comparing this to how QR codes or modern RAM use parity bits to detect and fix data corruption.
